conclusion: Pinned Skiko test TouchInjectionScope.cancel() clears only injector bookkeeping and does not deliver scene cancellation. The missing DragInteraction.Cancel in second/third diagnostics therefore did not prove a production detector defect.
test_correction: Test-only helper calls SkikoComposeUiTest.scene.cancelPointerInput after clearing touch injection. This is the production cancellation path used by the actual iOS mediator; no control callbacks or interaction events are fabricated. Disable/disposal/parent-consumption tests additionally exercise real event/node paths.
production_decision: Remove the attempted copied horizontal detector: the diagnostic did not justify a Foundation fork. Use stock public detectHorizontalDragGestures with owner cleanup on node reset/disposal. Keep the existing visual observer inner-finally cleanup without claiming the prior test verified it.
limitations: Test scene access opts in to InternalComposeUiApi; it is intentionally test-only and pinned to the declared Compose version.
Scene cancellation is not evidence of UIKit physical input delivery or device interoperability.
No new test result is claimed by this source inspection.
